topStories.headline: State Breaks Ground on $304M Juvenile Justice Facility Outside Waxahachie
topStories.dek: The Texas Juvenile Justice Department held a groundbreaking ceremony October 7 at 2278 FM 878 for a new 104-bed secure facility designed for youth with serious mental-health and behavioral needs.
topStories.body:
The Texas Juvenile Justice Department broke ground Wednesday, October 7, on a new state-operated secure juvenile correctional facility on the Ellis County Farm property at 2278 FM Road 878 in Waxahachie. The ceremony marked the second of two groundbreakings in as many weeks — a sister facility in Brazoria County broke ground October 1 — and signals the start of construction expected to be completed in the first half of 2029.

The Ellis County project is part of a $304 million investment authorized by the Texas Legislature during its 88th and 89th sessions. The two facilities together will add a combined 200 beds to the state's juvenile justice system. The Ellis County site is specifically designed to serve youth with the highest levels of mental and behavioral health needs, incorporating therapeutic environments and specialized programming including Mental Health Treatment Programs, a Behavioral Stabilization Unit, and a Crisis Stabilization Unit.

The project is being built under the oversight of the Texas Facilities Commission with architect HDR and construction partners Vaughn Construction and Kitchell. A public groundbreaking ceremony was held at 10 a.m. on October 7, where attendees heard from TJJD leadership, local officials, and legislative partners about the facility's design and purpose.

The new facility is located near the Ellis County Juvenile Services Building. Construction is now underway, with full occupancy targeted for early 2029.

topStories.headline: City Council Picks New Team to Revive Long-Vacant Downtown Police Building
topStories.dek: On a 4-1 vote October 6, the Waxahachie City Council authorized negotiations with Hart Systems Inc. for a Chapter 380 agreement to redevelop the former police headquarters at 216 N. College Street.
topStories.body:
Waxahachie's most persistently vacant downtown property may finally be on a path to new life. At its October 6 regular meeting, the City Council voted 4-1 to authorize the city to begin negotiations with Hart Systems Inc. — operators of a popular local restaurant — under a Chapter 380 economic development agreement for redevelopment of the city-owned former police building at 216 N. College Street.

The building has sat unused since 2018, and the city has pursued multiple development partners over the past several years without seeing the project through to completion. The most recent attempt, a food-hall concept called Waxahachie Social proposed by Ellis County Hospitality Group, halted earlier in 2026 after the developers could not meet a city-imposed construction-funding deadline.

The new partner, Hart Systems Inc., is described by the Waxahachie Daily Light as the operator of a popular local restaurant. A Chapter 380 agreement is a Texas economic development tool that allows cities to offer incentives such as sales-tax rebates in exchange for investment and job creation. Formal negotiations between the city and Hart Systems must now be concluded before any agreement is presented to the council for a final vote.

The council's next regular meeting is scheduled for Monday, October 19, at 7 p.m. at the Waxahachie Civic Center, 2000 Civic Center Lane.

topStories.headline: Council Accepts Federal Grant to Add 15 Firefighters to Waxahachie Fire-Rescue
topStories.dek: The Waxahachie City Council approved a federal SAFER grant at its October 6 meeting that will fund 15 additional positions for Waxahachie Fire-Rescue.
topStories.body:
Waxahachie Fire-Rescue is set to grow significantly after the City Council accepted a federal Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant at its October 6 regular meeting. The grant, administered through FEMA and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, is specifically designed to help fire departments hire and retain frontline firefighters.

The Waxahachie Daily Light reported that the council approved several items at the same meeting expected to improve the department's readiness. SAFER grants cover firefighter salaries and associated costs, with the goal of helping departments meet national staffing standards. The FEMA FY2025 SAFER program made $324 million available nationwide for fire departments.

Waxahachie Fire-Rescue currently operates out of four stations, serves a population of roughly 50,000 residents, and covers approximately 55 square miles within city limits. Adding 15 positions would represent a substantial increase to the department's frontline capacity. Details about the grant amount and the timeline for hiring were not publicly available from the paywalled news report, but the council action was confirmed in the October 5, 2026 edition of the Waxahachie Daily Light.

events.title: Farm Heritage Day at Ellis County Rural Heritage Farm (Rescheduled)
events.location: Ellis County Rural Heritage Farm, 130 Cunningham Meadows Road, Waxahachie
events.description: Originally scheduled for October 4 but postponed due to weather, this free community event features hayrides, farm animals, outdoor games, farm vendors, and farm living-history activities. Free admission, activities, and snacks (while supplies last, courtesy of H-E-B and AgTexas).

events.title: Stampede of Speed: Stars of Texas Music Festival
events.description: Three days of country music, bull riding, drag racing, BBQ, and lantern releases open the 10-day Stampede of Speed. The 2026 lineup features Aaron Watson (Friday), Brad Paisley (Saturday), and Travis Tritt (Sunday).

events.title: Stampede of Speed Fan Fest at Railyard Park (Free)
events.description: Meet NHRA and JEGS All-Star drivers at this free Fan Fest in downtown Waxahachie, featuring live music, free autographs, and a festival atmosphere. No ticket required.

events.title: Trunk-O-Palooza
events.description: Billed as the largest trunk-or-treat event in Texas, Trunk-O-Palooza is a family Halloween celebration hosted by the City of Waxahachie.

events.title: Crossroads of Texas GO TEXAN Country Festival
events.location: Historic Downtown Waxahachie, 100 W. Main St.
events.description: Texas' largest one-day arts, music, and food festival returns to the historic courthouse square with over 200 GO TEXAN-certified vendor booths, 10+ live music stages, and headliner Jake Worthington. Free admission.

events.title: Trick-or-Treat on the Square
events.description: The City of Waxahachie hosts its annual downtown trick-or-treat event on the courthouse square, with merchants handing out candy to kids in costume.

moreNews.headline: WISD Names Lumpkins Stadium Press Box After Longtime Trustee Dr. Joe Langley
moreNews.body: The Waxahachie Independent School District Board of Trustees voted at its regular meeting to name the press box at Lumpkins Stadium the Dr. Joe Langley Press Box, honoring the longtime board member's years of service to the district. Langley was recognized at the meeting, held in early October 2026. The Waxahachie Daily Light reported the honor on October 7, 2026.

moreNews.headline: Ellis County Burn Ban Remains in Effect
moreNews.body: Ellis County remains under a countywide burn ban first issued by the Commissioners' Court on July 21, 2026. The ban covers all unincorporated areas of the county and has not been lifted as of this week. Residents with questions should check the Ellis County official website for the latest status before conducting any outdoor burning.

moreNews.headline: Early Voting for November 3 General Election Opens October 19
moreNews.body: Ellis County voters have until October 19 to begin casting early ballots in the 2026 General and Special Elections, with early voting running through October 30. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Sample ballots and polling locations are available at elliscountytx.gov. The voter registration deadline for this election was October 5, 2026.
